subsystems.name: Optical sensor
subsystems.role: shines light into the skin and reads the faint Raman-scattered signal that carries chemical fingerprints.

subsystems.name: Interstitial fluid access
subsystems.role: brings the fluid between cells — which mirrors blood for many analytes — to the sensor without a needle.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and calibration
subsystems.role: turns overlapping raw spectra into concentration values for each substance.

subsystems.name: Wearable electronics and power
subsystems.role: runs the sensor, stores results, and sends them to a phone.

subsystems.name: User interface
subsystems.role: shows readings, trends and alerts to the wearer.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical path
buildSteps.detail: Choose laser wavelengths that penetrate skin deeply enough while keeping the Raman signal strong, and design a spectrometer small enough to wear but sensitive enough to detect trace analytes.

buildSteps.title: Create a non-invasive sampling method
buildSteps.detail: Develop an array of hollow microneedles that reach interstitial fluid without hitting nerves, or use a gentle electric current to draw glucose and other small molecules to the skin surface.

buildSteps.title: Build calibration models
buildSteps.detail: Collect thousands of paired measurements — Raman spectra or fluid samples alongside standard blood tests — to train algorithms that separate the signal of one substance from the background of skin, sweat and fat.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a wearable
buildSteps.detail: Combine the optical sensor, fluidic interface, electronics and battery into a device worn on the wrist or upper arm, keeping it comfortable and stable during movement.

buildSteps.title: Validate in clinical studies
buildSteps.detail: Test against laboratory blood draws in large, diverse groups, covering different skin tones, ages and health conditions, to prove accuracy and reliability.

buildSteps.title: Obtain regulatory approval
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate safety and clinical accuracy to medical regulators; this requires showing that the device matches blood tests within acceptable error margins.

buildSteps.title: Scale manufacturing
buildSteps.detail: Set up production lines for the microneedle arrays, optical components and sterile assembly, then launch with ongoing post-market monitoring.

prerequisites.why: handheld Raman analysers exist for materials and chemicals, but adapting them to sense trace analytes inside living skin is still a research challenge.
no approved device yet measures blood glucose reliably without piercing the skin; this is the hardest single-analyte case and a gateway to a broader health lab.

prerequisites.tech: Interstitial fluid sampling without a needle
prerequisites.why: current continuous glucose monitors use a filament inserted under the skin; truly non-invasive extraction is still in labs.
advanced algorithms can pull weak chemical signals out of noisy spectra, but they need large, diverse training sets that are still being gathered.
dissolving and coated microneedle patches are used for vaccination and some diagnostics, but continuous fluid sampling through them is not yet commercial.

pathway.milestone: laboratory studies measuring a single analyte such as glucose through skin in controlled conditions
pathway.unlocks: proof that the physics can work outside a test tube.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials of a wearable that tracks one analyte against blood draws
pathway.unlocks: regulatory clearance for a single-analyte device, likely glucose first.

pathway.milestone: expansion to multiple analytes — hormones, electrolytes, lactate — on the same platform
pathway.unlocks: a true personal health lab that can spot trends across several body systems.

pathway.milestone: integration with AI health coaching and remote clinical oversight
pathway.unlocks: early detection and management of metabolic and hormonal conditions from home.
